newsitem.title: USA: NASA astronaut trades space thrills for no frills.
newsitem.headline: NASA astronaut trades space thrills for no frills.

text.p: Veteran astronaut Robert "Hoot" Gibson has traded in the thrills of the U.S. space programme to become a pilot for a no-frills airline, a NASA spokeswoman said Thursday.

A veteran of five space shuttle missions and the first astronaut to dock the spacecraft with Russia's Mir space station, Gibson will leave NASA next week to join a training class for prospective Southwest Airlines Co. pilots.

Gibson, 50, announced plans to retire from the space agency on Wednesday. "While I am looking forward to new challenges and opportunities, I will certainly miss being a part of the NASA team," he said in a statement.

A former Navy test pilot, Gibson joined the astronaut corps in 1978, was chief astronaut until his June 1995 Mir docking mission and most recently was deputy director of flight crew operations at the Johnson Space Centre in Houston.

Next week, Gibson will begin building seniority needed to become a captain for Dallas-based Southwest, a pioneer low-fare carrier that labels small bags of peanuts "frills" to avoid being called a no-frills airline.
